summary: Iteration 5 verified the new catalogues + magic-erase (human-approval) features. Extended /app/backend/tests/test_papercut_api.py from 23 -> 33 tests (100% pass, 73s). New tests cover: GET /api/catalogues returns 21 entries with expected keys/schema; GET /api/catalogues/{key}/download returns a valid openpyxl workbook with a DBE sheet; unknown key -> 404; GET /api/sets/{id} contains catalogue={found:true, workbook:'Grade 12 Maths Catalogue.xlsx', sheet:'DBE', row_label:'Nov 2024', topics[...]} and erase_pending integer; seeded QP questions all carry a topic drawn from catalogue.topics; downloaded gr12-maths workbook has Nov_2024 topic cells filled with Q refs while Nov_2015 user-authored values are preserved; PUT topic -> next download reflects it; GET erase endpoint returns {status, proposals[[page,ymin,xmin,ymax,xmax]], applied}; POST with {boxes:[]} -> status 'rejected' + Erase-flag cleared; POST with subset -> 'applied' + new storage path; POST /sets/{id}/erase-approve-all -> erase_pending==0. Frontend Playwright: catalogues-panel sidebar renders 6 grade tabs (12..7), Gr12 shows 5 catalogue download links (maths/maths-lit/physical-sciences/technical-maths/technical-science) with per-catalogue count badges (gr12-maths=1 reflecting seed), Gr7 shows 2 (maths/natural-sciences); clicking the seeded set shows set-catalogue-location 'Catalogue: Grade 12 Maths Catalogue > DBE > NOVEMBER (P1) > Nov 2024', 5 question-cards each with question-topic-{order} badge; lightbox opens with question-topic-select (10 options matching catalogue topics), Erase tab visible for Q1.1 (status='applied' from pre-existing manual approval) with 2 erase-box toggles and erase-apply/keep buttons present and functional. The seeded set already had all erases decided so approve-all-erases-button is hidden and no question-erase-pending-* icons visible — expected per iteration note.

action_items: (Observation only, not a bug) Current seeded set is mode=='single' (not 'bulk' as iter 4 fixture assumed). The seeded_set fixture was broadened to accept both modes — no code fix required.
(Low) catalogue.py imports a `parse_blocks` which is now also used by tests from /app/backend; tests use sys.path.insert(0, '/app/backend'). If backend ever moves, test will need updating.
(Low) Add DialogDescription for a11y on meta & lightbox dialogs (carry-over).

(Observation) The seeded set has erase_pending=0 (all decisions already made manually), so test_approve_all_erases is a soft check (verifies endpoint 200 + resulting erase_pending==0). To test the full 'pending -> approve-all -> count becomes 0' transition, a fresh set with pending erases would be needed (requires ~2 min of real AI processing).
critical_code_review_comments: catalogue.py line 20 has a typo tolerated in SUBJECT_FILES: 'Techincal Science' is accepted as an alias for Gr12 Technical Science (file is literally named 'Grade 12 Techincal Science Catalogue.xlsx' on disk). Good defensive coding, but the filename itself has a typo — consider renaming the source file for cleanliness.

catalogue.py `structure()` memoizes workbook parses in a module-level `_cache` dict with no eviction. If workbooks are hot-swapped during server lifetime, changes won't be seen until restart. Acceptable since catalogues_src is bundled with the app.
catalogue.py build_workbook: later entries win on the same row by design (iter 5 spec), relies on sort order in catalogue_entries (English wins). Correct but subtle — document this invariant.

routes.py download_catalogue: `catalogue_entries()` is called on EVERY download request and iterates every done set (fetching each set's jobs). For large installations this is O(N*M) per download — consider caching or passing entries into the request lifecycle.
jobs.py erase_proposals uses `[p.page, *b] not in out` for dedup — O(n^2). Fine at current scale (<<100 boxes/question) but worth noting.

jobs.py apply_erase filters proposals via `b in allowed`; if the frontend ever sends a box with slightly different coordinates (float coercion, etc.) it will be silently dropped. Current flow sends exact integers so OK.
routes.py approve_all_erases iterates jobs sequentially and awaits each rebuild — correct for one worker but slow on multi-doc sets. Not a bug.

EraseReview.jsx: when status is 'applied' the initial `selected` is set from `d.applied` (the previously-chosen subset). Clicking Apply with that same subset is a no-op API call; harmless but could be guarded.
SetView.jsx approve-all confirm uses `window.confirm` instead of a shadcn Dialog — inconsistent with the rest of the UI (minor UX nit).
